subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should #91602 be split into separate reply-policy and process-control tracks, and should OpenClaw enforce terse action-only Telegram final replies by rewriting, suppressing, or annotating conversational closers?
rationale: Current source shows gaps, but choosing broad natural-language reply mutation and deciding whether raw shell `pkill` should be hardened or steered to managed `process kill` require product and owner-boundary judgment.

options.title: Split And Define Invariants
options.body: Track the follow-up-closing behavior with the #58450 policy family and the process-kill behavior with the #76259/#94697 family before implementation.

options.title: Require Live Repro First
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or QA run reproduces both the Telegram closing-question case and raw pkill abort on current main.

options.title: Accept Existing Mitigations
options.body: Keep the narrow reminder guard and managed process kill path as the intended behavior, accepting that this issue remains a product limitation rather than a core bug.

recommendation.title: Split And Define Invariants
recommendation.body: Track the follow-up-closing behavior with the #58450 policy family and the process-kill behavior with the #76259/#94697 family before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The main product decision extends the reminder guard and commitments behavior that vignesh07 introduced.
